daily_reality.summary: Paramedics provide advanced prehospital emergency medical care, responding to 911 calls, assessing patients, administering medications and advanced procedures (intubation, IV, EKG), and transporting patients to hospitals. They work 12-24 hour shifts in ambulances and fire stations.
typical_tasks: Assess patient condition and determine course of treatment
Administer CPR, defibrillation, and other life support
Perform advanced procedures: endotracheal intubation, IV access, medication administration
Use monitors, ventilators, and complex medical equipment
Stabilize and transport patients safely in ambulance
Transfer care to emergency department staff with verbal report
Document medical care given to patients (ePCR — electronic Patient Care Report)
Check emergency supplies, equipment, and drugs at start of shift
Decontaminate ambulance interior after contagious disease transport
Report communicable disease cases to authorities

deadlines.epcr_completion: Complete within shift or 24 hours per agency policy

daily_reality.seasonality: Holiday weekends, summer (trauma, drownings), winter (falls, cardiac events), and flu season see increased call volumes. Major events and heat waves create surge demand.

regulatory.summary: NREMT (National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians) provides national certification. All states require state licensure or certification with varying additional requirements. Scope of practice defined by National EMS Scope of Practice Model under medical director oversight.

key_laws.name: National EMS Scope of Practice Model
key_laws.detail: Federal framework defining paramedic scope including advanced airway, IV, medications, cardiac monitoring
key_laws.status: Current model, updated periodically by NHTSA

key_laws.name: State EMS Licensing Laws
key_laws.detail: Each state has own EMS licensing requirements, many accept NREMT as baseline

key_laws.name: Controlled Substance Regulations (DEA)
key_laws.detail: Paramedics carry and administer Schedule II-V medications under medical director DEA license

key_laws.name: HIPAA
key_laws.detail: Patient information protection for all ePCR and patient interactions

key_laws.name: Ryan White CARE Act (Notification provisions)
key_laws.detail: Requires notification of EMS personnel exposed to infectious diseases during patient care

requirements: Complete CAAHEP-accredited paramedic education program (1,200+ hours)
Pass NREMT Paramedic cognitive and psychomotor examinations
Apply for state licensure/certification (requirements vary by state)
60 hours continuing education every 2 years for NREMT recertification
National Continued Competency Program (NCCP) — national, local/state, and individual components
Medical director oversight required for clinical practice
certifying_bodies: NREMT — National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians
CAAHEP — Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs (program accreditation)

regulatory.penalties: State EMS office can suspend/revoke certification for negligence, substance abuse, or scope violations. HIPAA fines for patient data breaches. Controlled substance diversion is a federal crime.

tools.summary: Paramedics use advanced life support equipment including cardiac monitors/defibrillators (Zoll, Philips, Stryker), ventilators, drug boxes, IV pumps, and ePCR software (ImageTrend, ESO, Zoll RescueNet).

primary_software.name: Cardiac Monitor/Defibrillator (Zoll X Series, Philips MRx, Stryker LIFEPAK 15)
primary_software.purpose: 12-lead ECG, defibrillation, pacing, SpO2, ETCO2, BP monitoring

primary_software.name: ePCR Software (ImageTrend Elite, ESO, Zoll RescueNet)
primary_software.purpose: Electronic patient care reporting and documentation

primary_software.name: CAD Systems (Computer Aided Dispatch)
primary_software.purpose: Dispatch and routing for emergency calls

primary_software.name: Glucometers, iSTAT point-of-care analyzers
primary_software.purpose: Field blood glucose and blood chemistry testing

primary_software.name: Power stretchers (Stryker Power-PRO, Ferno)
primary_software.purpose: Patient transport with power loading systems

pain_points: Interoperability issues between CAD, ePCR, and hospital systems
Cost of equipment replacement and maintenance
Connectivity issues for electronic documentation in rural areas

terminology.summary: Paramedics use extensive medical and EMS-specific terminology including patient assessment language, cardiac rhythm interpretation, pharmacology, and radio communication codes.

key_terms.meaning: Advanced Cardiac Life Support — AHA protocol certification
ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction — heart attack requiring cath lab
End-tidal CO2 monitoring — confirms tube placement and ventilation
Intraosseous — bone marrow access for emergency medication/fluid delivery
Return of Spontaneous Circulation — after cardiac arrest resuscitation
Signs/Symptoms, Allergies, Medications, Past history, Last intake, Events — patient history mnemonic
Prioritizing patients by severity (START triage: red/yellow/green/black)
Emergency response with lights and sirens (varies by region)

career_psychology.summary: 76% of paramedics cite burnout as critical concern. High-stress, physically demanding work with life-and-death decisions. PTSD and substance abuse risks elevated. Career progression to flight medic, supervisor, educator, or fire officer.

career_levels.responsibilities: BLS care, patient assessment, CPR, basic airway
Full ALS scope, 12-lead, medications, advanced airway
Field Training Officer, complex calls, mentoring new medics
Shift supervision, QA/QI, protocol development, personnel management

main_fears: Making wrong treatment decisions in critical situations
PTSD from traumatic calls (shootings, MVAs, child abuse)
Certification loss for errors or substance abuse
Physical injury on scene (violence, vehicle accidents)
burnout_causes: Emotional toll of repeated traumatic calls
Low pay relative to training, responsibility, and risk
Physical demands: heavy lifting, awkward patient access
Lack of public appreciation and respect
growth_motivation: Fire officer track (in fire-based EMS systems)
Physician assistant or nursing school pathway

market.summary: Median salary $58,410 (BLS May 2024). 6% growth projected 2023-2033 with ~19,200 annual openings. About 168,800 paramedics employed. Severe staffing shortages driving overtime and burnout.
market.estimated_practitioners: ~168,800 paramedics employed in the US (BLS combined EMT/Paramedic category ~302,000)
market.job_outlook: 6% growth 2023-2033, faster than average. ~19,200 annual openings from growth and replacements.

work_arrangements.dominant: W-2 employees at municipal fire departments, private ambulance companies, hospitals
work_arrangements.private_ambulance: AMR, Acadian, Falck — largest private employers

market_trends: Severe staffing crisis driving wage increases
Community paramedicine/mobile integrated healthcare expanding scope
AI-assisted dispatch and decision support tools
